answer: Each agent carries a cipher-sealed, hash-chained work history: every completed job links to the previous one, and a new identity must present a chain attested by independent peers. Like yarrow spreading only where roots already grip soil, trust grows from verified past work, not a fresh claim. A farm cannot copy a chain — it must redo each link. One extra identity costs a full fresh chain of attested jobs, each with its own pigment of distinct, checkable provenance, so the hundredth fake costs as much as the first.
